The lineage of Bharata consists of these five meritorious branches, which are highly esteemed by the divine sages. **The Lineage of Bharata’s Descendants** Bharata had two wives: Mādhavī, the daughter of Yayāti, and Ātreyī, the daughter of Atri. Through Mādhavī, he begot Bhumanyu, while through Ātreyī, he begot Suhotra. Bhumanyu had two wives: Kāśeyī and Vaidarbhī. Through Kāśeyī, he begot Suhotra; and through Vaidarbhī, he begot Hastin. Hastin had two wives: Kāśeyī and Kausalyā. Through Kāśeyī, he begot Ajamīḍha, and through Kausalyā, he begot Nīla. Ajamīḍha had three wives: Keśinī, the daughter of Keśin; R̥kṣajā, the daughter of R̥kṣa; and Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of Druhyu. Through Keśinī, he begot Keśin; through R̥kṣajā, he begot R̥kṣa; and through Dhiṣaṇā, he begot Samvaraṇa. Samvaraṇa had one wife, Tapatī, the daughter of Vivasvat. From her, he begot Kuru. Kuru had four wives: Ātreyī, Prātīpa, Śubhā, and Vimalā. Through Ātreyī, he begot Āyu; through Prātīpa, he begot Devāpi; through Śubhā, he begot Śantanu; and through Vimalā, he begot Bahulāśva. Āyu had two wives: Sudevā and Pauravī. Through Sudevā, he begot Raudrāśva; and through Pauravī, he begot Bṛhatkṣatra. Bṛhatkṣatra had two wives: Kāśeyī and Kausalyā. Through Kāśeyī, he begot Caṇḍanu; and through Kausalyā, he begot Suhotra. Suhotra had two wives: Kāśeyī and Kausalyā. Through Kāśeyī, he begot Hasti; and through Kausalyā, he begot Vicitravīrya. Vicitravīrya had two wives: Ambikā and Ambālikā. Through them, he begot Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu. Dhṛtarāṣṭra had one wife, Gāndhārī, the daughter of Subala. From her, he begot a hundred sons, of whom Duryodhana was the eldest. Pāṇḍu had two wives: Kuntī and Mādrī.
